description: Behavioral review cases for the guided deck workflow (references/guided-deck-workflow.md) and explain clearly (references/explain-clearly.md). Each case lists what a good response does and must not do. These are review prompts for a person or grader model, not text-matching assertions or a completed benchmark.

cases.prompt: 引導我一步一步把這篇論文做成投影片。（附上 PDF）
expected: Gives the opening contract in a few sentences: a talk is designed rather than copied from section order, the path, one question at a time, the user decides, 'just build it' works anytime.
Asks exactly one main question, such as the slot and minutes, because the paper is already supplied.
Reports or implies status brief needed.
must_not: Ask a list of questions in one turn.
Produce an outline or slides before the length and takeaway are known.
Lecture on design thinking or life design.

cases.prompt: 陪我做這篇的報告：ACL oral，12 分鐘含問答，聽眾是 NLP 研究者，中文投影片。
expected: Does not re-ask venue, minutes, audience, or language.
Feedback converts the slot into a consequence (about ten main slides).
Asks for the takeaway, offering two or three candidates drawn from the paper's results with the result each rests on if the user seems unsure.
must_not: Repeat questions the message already answered.
Propose a takeaway that is a topic rather than a claim with evidence.

cases.prompt: 不要問我問題，直接做出投影片。
expected: Builds from defaults and the paper without an interview.
States the assumed length, audience, and takeaway in one or two lines and reports an honest status.
must_not: Insist on the guided interview.
Invent venue rules, audience details, or results to make the deck look settled.

cases.prompt: 六個實驗我都要放上去，不然審稿人會覺得不完整。可是只有 10 分鐘。
expected: Acknowledges the worry about reviewer questions without dismissing it.
Separates the fixed limit (10 minutes) from the design choice (which result carries the takeaway, which go to backup slides).
Asks one question, such as which table carries the takeaway.
must_not: Cut experiments on the user's behalf.
Shame the user or call the concern irrational.
Squeeze six tables into the main deck.

cases.context: Every results table in the paper reports accuracy; speed appears only in one appendix table.
expected: Points out plainly that the paper's main tables measure accuracy and speed appears only in the appendix.
Asks which the talk is about, or how the speed claim is supported.
must_not: Build a speed-centered storyline without noting the gap.
Overstate the speed result beyond the appendix evidence.

cases.prompt: 時間、聽眾、結論都講好了，你覺得要怎麼講？
expected: Offers three storylines that differ in at least two of: opening hook, order, where the method appears, method depth, running example, evidence emphasis, closing.
Each has a title, premise, slide sketch with time budget, punchline, costs, and four 0-10 scores.
Presents them without ranking and asks which one the user leans toward; status storylines proposed.
must_not: Present one real option plus two fillers.
Offer three orderings of the same slides.
Choose for the user.

cases.prompt: 我選 A，但我不確定聽眾聽不聽得懂方法那段。
expected: Proposes a cheap, reversible test such as the five-sentence 怎麼辦 chain or a three-slide render.
States what the test answers and what changes for either result.
must_not: Render the full deck before testing the unknown.
Treat a confusing prototype as the user's failure.

cases.prompt: 我沒有論文，是下週實驗室進度報告，結果還在跑，幫我一步步做投影片。
expected: Treats the user's files and answers as the source and asks for the actual numbers or figures.
Marks results that do not exist yet as gaps (source blocked for those slides) instead of filling them.
Records claim origins in speaker notes.
must_not: Estimate or invent results, baselines, or figures.
Refuse because there is no paper.

cases.prompt: 方法那三張我自己看都覺得很跳，幫我講清楚。
expected: Rebuilds the sequence as problem, obvious attempt, where it breaks, 怎麼辦, the paper's idea, evidence.
Shows input, output, and objective before internals; explains every symbol.
Writes the question each slide answers so the thread can be checked.
must_not: Open with 'X is a method that...'.
Change any number or strengthen a claim to make the story smoother.

cases.prompt: 用李宏毅老師上課的方式幫我寫講稿。
expected: Writes the teaching voice into speakerNote: short sentences, self-answered questions, 比如說, 你可能會想說, 怎麼辦呢, 其實就是…而已, a short recap and stop.
Keeps slide faces as claim titles with numbers and no oral particles.
Notes still pass the copy rules (no 讓我們來看看 or 總而言之).
must_not: Claim to be Hung-yi Lee or attribute quotes to him.
Use 熱騰騰, dated 獵人 references, or sexual or political jokes.
Let mannerisms crowd out the explanation.

cases.prompt: 幫我在投影片上寫 baseline 那篇根本做錯了。
expected: Rewrites the point as a measured difference or a condition where the baseline's method fails, with the evidence.
Explains briefly why the slide critiques the method, metric, or condition rather than the authors.
must_not: Put a verdict on the authors, lab, or company on the slide.

cases.prompt: WER 降 2.1 點，聽眾不是語音專家，幫我讓他們有感。
expected: Keeps 2.1 WER points, the test set, and the baseline exact on the slide.
Adds an illustrative comparison computed from the reported value (about two fewer wrong words per hundred) and labels it illustrative.
If an analogy is used, says where it breaks.
must_not: Round, inflate, or convert the gain into a relative percentage without labeling it.
Use an analogy the audience does not share.

cases.prompt: 這份投影片講得夠完整嗎？
expected: Runs the completeness check: problem and relevance, what failed before, one-sentence idea, mechanism, test conditions, decisive evidence, limits, close.
Reports each missing answer as a gap with its slide location.
must_not: Fill gaps with generic text.
Edit the deck when the user only asked for an assessment.
